description: METER, the MEthane Tracking Emissions Reference, is a global database of infrastructure that emits methane, released in February 2026 by a Stanford University team including Robert Jackson and Andrew Ng. The Zenodo record read on 2026-09-28 describes it as a publicly available database designed as a platform that users can extend with new datasets, and its keywords name oil and natural gas facilities, coal mines, landfills, wastewater plants and power plants. Coverage is global. The record states a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence, but the deposit is marked restricted and its file listing returned "permission denied", so the data must be requested and its format, attributes and number of assets are unknown. Caveats: the description is only one sentence, there is no linked paper in the metadata, and the restricted status conflicts with the "publicly available" wording, so availability should be checked before planning on it. It supports environmental impact and exposure studies of energy and waste infrastructure, such as locating landfills, wastewater plants and gas facilities for methane mitigation or overlaying them on flood and heat hazard maps. No related methane infrastructure database record is catalogued.
